result:
All three findings are fixed and tested, but one required check is incomplete: the full `pnpm test:integration` has not passed on the final code. My one full run crashed after 14 of about 384 files (its worker died, most likely out of memory, while other runs shared the machine). There wasn't time for a fresh one, so please run it at integration. I finished at 23:19:51 UTC, about 12 minutes past the 2-hour limit. All changes are uncommitted.

**The fix.** One shared helper, `apps/api/src/modules/access/sensitive-reach.ts`, decides for any record whether it reveals a sensitive benefit, business case or evidence item the caller may not open. That covers the record itself and the rows that hold its values: measurements, plan values, business-case lines, evidence links, form comments and attachments, and the sensitivity flag and grants. Every affected route calls it; there are no per-route copies.

| Finding | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| F-DG6-121 (`/transformations/{id}/audit`) | The route returned every event with no sensitivity check. | Events of a hidden record and of its child rows now come back with `changes` and `reason` null. Actor, action, time, record id and versions stay. |
| F-DG6-122 (`/audit-events`) | It used a temporary rule that only matched an event's own record, so child events leaked (and admitted users were over-redacted). | The temporary rule is deleted and the shared helper is wired in. Child events are redacted; grantees, named parties and TO see everything. |
| F-DG6-123 (T14 form-record routes) | The shared form read gate and the writes only checked transformation access and existence. | One gate in `forms/record-types.ts` now covers versions, compare, comments (read and write), attachments, custom fields, bulk edit, reference checks, draft creation and the T14 export. |

**Other gaps closed by the route sweep:**
- `GET /benefit-measurements/{id}` and `GET /benefit-plan-values/{id}` had no sensitivity check. They are now covered by a small pre-handler on child-record path parameters, which also covers six other child item routes.
- The transformation-level lists of finance validations, overlaps and scenarios now leave out hidden rows.

The handback lists every route I checked.

**Tests.** The new `apps/api/test/integration/access/sensitive-reach.test.ts` has 10 cases covering TL, AUD and TO, plus the owner, with and without a grant, allowed and denied.
- Before the fix: 6 failed, exactly the leak cases.
- After the fix: 10 passed.
- The reviewer's two reproduction tests, run temporarily, now fail at exactly their leak assertions, which is the expected result.

**Checks on the final code:**
- **Unit tests:** `pnpm test` exits 0 with the locale unset and with C.UTF-8 (2817 + 2018 + 259 passed, 2 skipped, in each).
- **Integration:** a targeted run passed, 40 files with 602 tests. It covered the access, audit, forms, evidence and benefits directories and the sensitive-record test in `tests/qa`. `contract.test.ts` alone passed 105/105.
- **Typecheck and lint:** API typecheck exit 0; ESLint on the changed files exit 0.
- **Validator:** DG5 historical passed at the start and the end.
- **Ran before my last three edits to the helper:** the full typecheck, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm -r build`, the Prettier check and `openapi:lint` all exited 0 then, but I didn't re-run them after.

**Failures along the way, all in the handback:**
- The typecheck was killed twice for lack of memory (exit 137) while tests ran alongside it.
- My first version of the guard also covered evidence ids. That turned the evidence download's declared 403 into a 404 and broke two contract exercises and one `tests/qa` test, so I removed evidence from the guard.
- A later refactor broke the flag and comment lookup. The targeted run caught it and it is fixed.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Finance on sensitive benefits:** a Finance user who is neither the benefit's named validator nor a grantee now gets 404 on that benefit's finance validations. That follows ADR-0051 §2 literally, but it means a sensitive benefit's validation needs a named validator or a grant. Domain review should confirm this.
- **Redaction label on the per-transformation audit:** `AuditEvent` could gain an optional `redacted` field so the per-transformation audit page can show a "Redacted" label. I didn't add it because the contract is shared with the concurrent tasks; null values already conform.

**Not done:**
- Scenario list items can still embed a value of a sensitive benefit when the scenario's own business case isn't sensitive.
- Corrective cases, transition decisions and performance-area links are redacted in the audit, but their own register routes are not hidden. Whether ADR-0051 §2 should extend to them is a domain question.

No migration, no new dependency, no new or changed operations (pending list unchanged), and no user-facing text made untrue.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/`:
- T-DG6-BE-Y1-backend-workflow-engineer.md
- T-DG6-BE-Y1-evidence/
